title: Site construction for the closed complement of a subterminal sheaf
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-topos] with finite limits, terminal object $X$, and subcanonical topology, meaning that every presheaf $h_V(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(W,V)$ is a $J$-sheaf. Let $U\to X$ be a monomorphism and set $F=h_U\hookrightarrow h_X=1$. On the same underlying category define a family $\{V_i\to V\}$ to cover for $J_c$ precisely when the family $\{V_i\to V\}\cup\{U\times_XV\to V\}$ is $J$-covering (a family is covering when its generated sieve is covering). These families define a Grothendieck topology $J_c$. The identity on underlying presheaves defines a fully faithful functor $I:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J_c)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J)$. It is the direct image of a geometric morphism $q$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism], and its essential image consists exactly of the $J$-sheaves $G$ such that $F\times G\to F$ is an isomorphism. All representables in this statement are sheaves for $J$; no subcanonicity of $J_c$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 08LY (lemma-closed-subtopos), modified covering construction and essential-image identification, on the subcanonical finite-limit site chosen at the start of its proof.

proof.text: For each object $V$ put $o_V:U\times_XV\to V$ and let $O_V$ be the sieve of arrows factoring through $o_V$. The pullback universal property says that $f:W\to V$ belongs to $O_V$ exactly when $W$ admits a map to $U$: together with $f$, such a map gives the required factorization. There is at most one map $W\to U$, since $U\to X$ is mono and $X$ is terminal. Consequently, for every $a:W\to V$, $a^*O_V=O_W$. For a sieve $R$ on $V$ define $R\in J_c(V)$ to mean $R\cup O_V\in J(V)$. Unions here are unions of the sets of arrows, hence are sieves, and pullback distributes over these unions. All these collections are small because the objects and arrows of $\mathcal C$ form sets.

source.place: Tag 08LY (lemma-closed-subtopos), modified covering construction; sieve formulation using Tag 00Z4 (definition-topology).

proof.text: We check the three topology axioms of [def-weil-pbc-topos]. The maximal sieve belongs to $J_c$. If $R\cup O_V$ is $J$-covering, then $a^*R\cup O_W=a^*(R\cup O_V)$ is $J$-covering, so pullback stability holds. For transitivity, suppose $S\in J_c(V)$ and $f^*R\in J_c(W)$ for every $f:W\to V$ in $S$. Set $T=R\cup O_V$. The sieve $S\cup O_V$ is $J$-covering. For $f\in S$, $f^*T=f^*R\cup O_W$ is $J$-covering by hypothesis; for $f\in O_V$, $f\in T$, so $f^*T$ is maximal. The transitivity axiom for $J$ applied to $S\cup O_V$ therefore gives $T\in J(V)$, which is $R\in J_c(V)$. Thus $J_c$ is a Grothendieck topology.

source.place: Tag 08LY (lemma-closed-subtopos), verification of the site axioms; direct verification of the sieve axioms of Tag 00Z4.

proof.text: If $R$ is generated by a family $\{V_i\to V\}$, then $R\cup O_V$ is generated by that family together with $o_V$. Hence the topology just constructed gives exactly the covering families in the statement. For either topology, these generated-sieve covering families form a covering-family site: an isomorphism generates the maximal sieve; the sieve generated by a pulled-back family is the pullback of the generated sieve, since all fibre products exist; for composed covering families, the pullback of the composite sieve along each first-family arrow contains the second-family covering sieve, and topology transitivity gives a covering composite. Upward closure used here follows directly from the topology axioms: if $S\subseteq T$ and $S$ covers, then $f^*T$ is maximal for every $f\in S$. The sieve and family sheaf conditions agree directly: a compatible family on generating arrows extends to their generated sieve by restriction, with independence of a chosen factorization checked on the fibre product of two generating domains. Conversely a matching family on a sieve restricts to its arrows viewed as a covering family. Finally $J\subseteq J_c$ by upward closure, so a $J_c$-sheaf is a $J$-sheaf. The functor $I$ acts identically on underlying presheaves and natural transformations. Both sheaf categories are full presheaf subcategories, so $I$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 08LY (lemma-closed-subtopos), identity direct image; Tag 00Z4 and the generated-sieve covering convention in the item.

proof.text: For a J-sheaf G, the projection h_U × G → h_U is invertible exactly when G(W) is a singleton for every W admitting a map to U. Prove this by Yoneda and the product universal property: if the projection is invertible, compose a morphism h_W → h_U with its inverse and the second projection to obtain the unique map h_W → G. Conversely choose the unique section on each W mapping to U; uniqueness proves naturality and gives h_U → G. Pair this with the identity of h_U to construct the inverse of the projection; the second inverse identity follows componentwise from uniqueness. No choice of a sectionwise product model is needed.

source.place: Tag 08LY (lemma-closed-subtopos), essential-image criterion; Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf) for sectionwise products.

proof.text: Let $G$ be a $J_c$-sheaf. If $W$ admits a map to $U$, the inverse constructed in step 4 makes $o_W:U\times_XW\to W$ an isomorphism. Thus $O_W$ is maximal and the empty sieve is $J_c$-covering on $W$. Its unique-amalgamation sheaf condition in [def-weil-pbc-topos] says precisely that $G(W)$ is a singleton: the empty matching family has exactly one amalgamation. By step 3, $IG$ is a $J$-sheaf, and by step 4 it satisfies $F\times IG\cong F$.

source.place: Tag 08LY (lemma-closed-subtopos), last sentence: the empty cover on the open locus.

proof.text: Conversely let $G$ be a $J$-sheaf satisfying $F\times G\cong F$. Fix $R\in J_c(V)$ and a matching family $(s_f)_{f\in R}$ in $G$. By step 4, $G(W)$ is a singleton for every domain $W$ of an arrow in $O_V$. Extend the family to $T=R\cup O_V$ by assigning to each $f:W\to V$ in $O_V$ that unique element of $G(W)$. On $R\cap O_V$ this agrees with $s_f$. Compatibility for an arrow in $R$ and its restrictions is the given matching condition. For an arrow in $O_V$, every restricted domain also maps to $U$, and both required sections lie in a singleton, so compatibility holds. These observations also handle a restricted arrow lying in both sieves. Since $T$ is $J$-covering, there is a unique $s\in G(V)$ amalgamating the extended family. It amalgamates the original family on $R$. If another section amalgamates on $R$, its restrictions to every arrow in $O_V$ necessarily equal the unique sections there; hence it too amalgamates on $T$ and equals $s$. Therefore $G$ satisfies the $J_c$-sheaf condition for every covering sieve. Together with step 5 this proves the asserted essential-image equality, including objects isomorphic to image objects since the projection property is invariant under isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08LY (lemma-closed-subtopos), the omitted argument that a sheaf terminal on the open satisfies the finer sheaf condition; details supplied here.

proof.text: Let I be the fully faithful identity-on-presheaves inclusion constructed in step 3, and let L be the composite of the inclusion Sh(C,J) → PSh(C) and J_c-sheafification. Restrict the sheafification adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] along the fully faithful inclusion Sh(C,J) → PSh(C). Both comparison isomorphisms are identity isomorphisms, since I does not change presheaves or their maps. Mathlib Adjunction.restrictFullyFaithful therefore supplies L ⊣ I directly, without a left Kan extension.

source.place: Tag 08LY (lemma-closed-subtopos), construction of the site morphism; Tag 00WX (lemma-adjoint-sheaves) and Tag 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), identity-functor specialization.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], finite limits in $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J)$ are the underlying presheaf limits. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], sheafification for the small site $(\mathcal C,J_c)$ preserves finite limits. Consequently the functor $L$ of step 7 preserves finite limits. Each sheaf category is a Grothendieck topos by its small-site presentation [def-weil-pbc-topos]. The adjunction $L\dashv I$ therefore defines a geometric morphism $q:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J_c)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J)$ in [def-trf-geometric-morphism], with $q_*=I$. Steps 3 and 5–6 give its full faithfulness and exactly its required essential image. No step requires representables to be sheaves for $J_c$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08LY (lemma-closed-subtopos): modified topology, empty-cover and matching-family gluing arguments implemented directly. The projection criterion uses Yoneda and the binary-product universal property. lean.statement: theorem closed_complement_site_construction (C : Type w) [SmallCategory C] [HasFiniteLimits C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) [J.Subcanonical] (X : C) (hX : IsTerminal X) (U : C) (i : U ⟶ X) [Mono i] : ∃ Jc : GrothendieckTopology C, (∀ (V : C) (R : Presieve V), Sieve.generate R ∈ Jc V ↔ Sieve.generate (R ⊔ Presieve.singleton (pullback.snd i (hX.from V))) ∈ J V) ∧ ∃ q : GeometricMorphism (Sheaf Jc (Type w)) (Sheaf J (Type w)), q.direct ⋙ sheafToPresheaf J (Type w) = sheafToPresheaf Jc (Type w) ∧ Nonempty q.direct.FullyFaithful ∧ ∀ G : Sheaf J (Type w), q.direct.essImage G ↔ IsIso (prod.fst : J.yoneda.obj U ⨯ G ⟶ J.yoneda.obj U)
